macroscopy: Thin greenish leaflets with characteristic venation.
microscopy: Dorsiventral leaflet with characteristic epidermal and stomatal features.
adverse_effects: Cramping, diarrhoea and electrolyte disturbances with excessive use.
contraindications: Intestinal obstruction and acute inflammatory abdominal conditions.
adulterants: Other Senna species or non-official leaflets.

macroscopy: Yellowish-brown root with yellow interior and sweet taste.
microscopy: Cork, secondary phloem, medullary rays and calcium oxalate features.
pharmacological_action: Demulcent and expectorant properties; high exposure may produce mineralocorticoid-like effects.
uses: Symptomatic cough and dyspeptic complaints in appropriate preparations.
adverse_effects: Sodium retention, hypokalaemia and hypertension with excessive/prolonged use.
contraindications: Severe hypertension, hypokalaemia and sodium-retention states.
adulterants: Other Glycyrrhiza species or exhausted material.
